Field notes 01 · 20 May 2026

Values can be right and still fail in execution

On the translation layer between the people setting direction and the people expected to make it real.

Values can be right and still fail in execution. The issue is often not what was said at the top, but what the system was able to do with it.

Senior teams often see where the organisation needs to go. They send the message down through town halls, emails, training and leadership decks. Usually with serious intent.

What often stays unchecked is more basic. Whether local leaders understood what they are now expected to carry. Whether people can act on it inside the constraints, incentives and decision habits that still govern the work. Often they cannot.

The organisation appears aligned in the reporting, but behaves otherwise. Decisions are agreed, then reopened a few weeks later. Priorities are repeated, but interpreted differently from site to site. Local leaders pass on language they cannot fully use, to teams already stretched too thin.

Some local leaders feel trapped between what they are asked to say and what the system still allows them to do. Teams keep delivery moving through workarounds that often look like the only way forward. Reports stay acceptable long after reality has moved.

None of this is sabotage. For a while, results can even improve. People work at 200% to hold the system together. The change has not landed, but the effort to compensate looks like progress.

The cost appears later, in burnout, quiet exits and loss of trust in the programme. Then the diagnosis blames the people. “Resistance to change.” “Capability gaps.” “Poor adoption.” Sometimes the diagnosis is too easy.

The values are right. The strategy may be right. What failed is the translation layer between the people setting direction and the people expected to make it real. This is not only a communication problem. It is an operational loss of meaning between levels of the organisation.

We work on both sides until what was said at the top means the same thing where the work happens.

This is the kind of drift we work on at DRIFT Partners.

Anna Chodynicka, DRIFT Partners · First published 20 May 2026
